_readme: Divergences between a hand-written fake and the recorded wire contract that
were reviewed and found to be gaps in the RECORDING, not defects in the fake.
A contract records what was observed. The live suite works on a sandbox it
builds itself — an empty cube, a two-element dimension, a process with no
data source — and the read sweep walks whatever model happens to be on the
server. Shapes that neither produced were never recorded, even though TM1
Every entry below states why the fake is right. Anything not listed here
fails the build, so an invented field still cannot slip through. Each entry
is also a to-do: widen the recording until the exception is unnecessary,
Fields: endpoint (contract key), path (payload path, array indices

exceptions.reason: Present only on entries that carry detail rows. The test server's audit log had none during recording; TM1 expands AuditDetails whenever the entry has them.
ViewService.list requests $select=Name,MDX; the recording's list calls selected Name only, so the column never appeared. MDX is a real View property.
Null for a native view — the recorded views were all MDX views, so only the string branch was seen. A native view legitimately returns MDX: null.
Only consolidated elements have Children, and only when the query expands them. The swept models exposed leaves at the sampled positions.
Level is a standard Element property; the DefaultMember probe in the recording used a narrower $select.
Standard Element property, omitted by the $select used on the recorded call path.
Navigation property expanded only by some call paths; the recorded Elements calls did not expand it. Its shape IS recorded under the Hierarchies endpoint.
ASCII data-source field. TM1's DataSource properties are camelCase in the OData model; no recorded process used an ASCII source.
ASCII data-source field; see asciiDelimiterChar.
ASCII data-source field; see asciiDelimiterChar.
Set on file and ODBC sources. The recorded processes had DataSource type None.
Set on file and ODBC sources; see dataSourceNameForClient.
ODBC-only field. No ODBC process existed on either recorded server.
ODBC-only field; see oDBCConnection.
A TI parameter's default is numeric or string depending on its type. Only numeric defaults were recorded; the string branch is equally valid.
Returned only when the run produced an error log. The recorded executions succeeded.

One test deliberately feeds the nested `{value: ...}` error shape, which http.ts accepts alongside the plain string. No recorded server sends it; the test exists to pin that tolerance, so the divergence from the contract is the point.

Several BatchService tests answer a $batch POST with a deliberately NON-envelope 200 (a proxy or misconfigured gateway returning a page, `{nope:true}`, …). Violating the contract is the scenario under test, not a defective fake, and the payload differs per case — hence the wildcard path.
getAllRules is overloaded: without `top` it returns CubeRules[], with `top` it returns {items,total}. The live suite only calls the unpaginated form, so the paginated shape was never recorded.
Paginated overload of getAllRules; see $.items.
Set only when the run produced an error log. The recorded executions either succeeded or failed without one, so the key was never observed carrying a value.
ODBC-only field; no ODBC process existed on either recorded server. Mirrors the wire-level exception on GET /api/v1/Processes('*').
ODBC/file credential field; see $.oDBCConnection.
Set on file and ODBC sources; the recorded processes had DataSource type None.
A TI parameter default is numeric or string depending on the parameter's type. Only numeric defaults were recorded.
Present only when service authentication is configured. The masking test needs the key to exist in order to prove it gets masked.
Present only when LDAP is configured; see ServiceAuthPassword. Neither recorded server used LDAP.
Credential field on file and ODBC sources. The recorded processes had DataSource type None, so it never appeared — and the test that needs it is precisely the one proving the password gets masked.
